title: Hungarian Beef Goulash
description: A soup-thick stew built on collapsed onions and a lot of paprika, cooked long enough that the shin turns to gelatin. Makes a full pot and reheats better than it serves.
notes: Paprika is the ingredient, not the seasoning — buy it fresh and in quantity. A tin that has been open since last winter tastes of dust and no amount of it will fix the pot.

steps.text: Cook the sliced onions in the lard over low heat until they lose every trace of structure and slump into a soft golden mass.
steps.tip: Half an hour looks absurd for onions and it is not negotiable. This is the body of the finished stew — hurry it and you get flavoured water.

steps.text: Pull the pot off the heat entirely. Stir the sweet paprika and the hot paprika through the onions away from the flame, then set it back on the lowest burner.
steps.tip: Paprika scorches at frying temperature in about ten seconds and the bitterness never cooks out.

steps.text: Add the beef shin, caraway seeds, garlic, salt, and black pepper, and turn the meat until every cube is red.
Pour in enough beef stock to barely cover the meat, bring it to a lazy simmer, and cook covered until a cube gives way under a spoon.
steps.tip: Barely covered, not swimming. You want to end up with a thick pot, and you cannot boil liquid off a stew without overcooking the meat.

steps.text: Add the green peppers, tomatoes, and potatoes and simmer uncovered until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has pulled together.
Rest the pot off the heat before serving, then taste again — it will take more salt cold than it did hot.
